conflicts.description: The same patient entity is named patients in Synthea and person in OMOP, with corresponding attribute synonyms such as id/person_id, birthdate/birth_datetime, and gender/gender_source_value.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted the singular canonical person resource and explicit snake_case attribute names while retaining standard-concept and source-value representations separately.

conflicts.description: Synthea calls a care interaction an encounter while OMOP calls the comparable top-level event a visit occurrence.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted encounter as the canonical business term and aligned only semantically equivalent top-level visit attributes.

conflicts.description: Provider specialty uses a misspelled Synthea column and OMOP source-value terminology.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the target spelling to specialty and retained separate standard-concept and source-value columns.

conflicts.description: Several Synthea field names contain spaces and are not snake_case.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed them to atomic snake_case source-value and description fields.

conflicts.description: Monetary values are represented primarily as strings, despite being quantitative amounts.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized monetary amounts to number; currency remains an independent concept attribute.

conflicts.description: Synthea declares observation type as number even though it describes a datatype, and stores heterogeneous result values in one string column; OMOP separates numeric, text, and concept results.
conflicts.resolution: Represented the datatype indicator as string and split results into numeric, textual, concept, and verbatim source-value fields.

conflicts.description: Fields described as timestamps are typed as date in both sources.
conflicts.resolution: Used datetime for canonical event timestamps while allowing date-only source precision.

conflicts.description: Invalidation reason flags are incorrectly typed as date in several OMOP resources.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled invalidation reasons as strings and kept validity dates in separate date fields.

conflicts.description: Coordinates and numeric reference-range limits are represented as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized these quantitative values to number.

conflicts.description: Textual values are incorrectly declared as integer in the source schema.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical textual counterparts use string; composite NLP modifiers should be normalized when those extensions are materialized.

conflicts.description: Synthea code columns contain vocabulary-native codes, whereas OMOP distinguishes globally unique standard concept identifiers from verbatim source codes.
conflicts.resolution: Kept standard concept identifiers, source concept identifiers, and source values as distinct semantic attributes; vocabulary-native codes were never merged directly into concept IDs.

conflicts.description: Units may be free text in Synthea but standardized concepts plus source text in OMOP, and physical quantities may use non-SI scales.
conflicts.resolution: Retained both standard unit concepts and source unit text; canonical numeric values and ranges are to be expressed in compatible SI units where a valid conversion exists.

conflicts.description: The Synthea encounter provider field is documented as an organization foreign key, while OMOP provider_id identifies a clinician.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped Synthea encounters.provider only to care_site_id and kept clinician provider_id semantically separate.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses compact M/F source encoding while OMOP distinguishes source encoding from standardized gender concepts.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved the source value and provided a separate FK to the standardized concept.

conflicts.description: Synthea base or line-item cost does not specify whether the amount is a charge, provider cost, or paid amount, while OMOP distinguishes these semantics.
conflicts.resolution: Stored Synthea amounts in a dedicated base_or_line_item_amount field and did not merge them with OMOP total charge, cost, or paid fields.

conflicts.description: Synthea repeats address attributes in entity tables, while OMOP normalizes geographic data into location.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted a normalized location resource and location foreign keys; generated location identifiers are used where Synthea has no source location key.

conflicts.description: Synthea combines labs and general observations in one table, while OMOP decomposes them into observation and measurement domains.
conflicts.resolution: Created one canonical clinical_observation resource with an explicit domain discriminator and homogeneous result fields, preserving the source domain without conflating identifiers.

conflicts.description: Synthea embeds cost on clinical event rows, while OMOP stores costs in a separate event-linked table.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized costs into event_cost so each monetary record is related to its clinical event rather than embedded in multiple event structures.

conflicts.description: Synthea embeds death date in the patient row, while OMOP uses a separate death resource with cause and provenance attributes.
conflicts.resolution: Placed the shared death date on person for the core unified view; OMOP-specific cause and death-provenance details remain separable extensions and are not conflated with demographics.

conflicts.description: Synthea provides a dedicated imaging-study structure, whereas OMOP can represent imaging through multiple clinical domains and lacks a directly equivalent study-series table in the supplied package.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved imaging_study as a dedicated normalized resource rather than forcing non-equivalent OMOP event fields into it.

conflicts.description: Synthea has one encounter level, whereas OMOP supports a visit occurrence with zero or more nested visit details.
conflicts.resolution: Unified Synthea encounters with the top-level OMOP visit occurrence; nested visit details remain a subordinate extension and are not merged into the encounter identity.

conflicts.description: Both models support many providers per organization/care site, but Synthea embeds addresses on both entities while OMOP generally associates providers with a care site.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled provider-to-care-site as N:1 and separated optional provider and care-site locations.

conflicts.description: A person and encounter can have many heterogeneous result records; source decomposition differs by domain.
conflicts.resolution: Used a 1:N relationship from person and encounter to clinical_observation, with one row per atomic result.

conflicts.description: OMOP contains multiple many-to-many semantic and fact relationship structures with directional roles.
conflicts.resolution: These relationship roles must remain bridge structures with separate source and destination foreign keys; their identifiers are never coalesced into one provenance-bearing field.

conflicts.description: Several Synthea event tables declare no primary key, while comparable OMOP event tables contain event identifiers that are not consistently declared as primary keys in the supplied package.
conflicts.resolution: Declared canonical event primary keys; used OMOP identifiers where available and synthetic keys only for Synthea rows without source identifiers.

conflicts.description: Equivalent person identities use different key names.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them as person.person_id and listed both source primary-key columns in provenance.

conflicts.description: Equivalent top-level encounter identities use different key names.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them as encounter.encounter_id and listed both source keys in provenance.

conflicts.description: Identically suggestive foreign-key names refer to different entity types: organization in Synthea and clinician in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Kept care_site_id and provider_id as separate foreign keys and prohibited identity coalescence.

conflicts.description: Several OMOP fields are polymorphic references whose target table is determined by an accompanying domain or field concept rather than a conventional foreign key.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved the conceptual polymorphism for extension resources and did not incorrectly declare these IDs as foreign keys to one canonical entity.
